title: A Will for the Ledger
premise: When the coffin of Ashfall's founder, Cornelius Vane, is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, insurance investigator Gideon Yarrow is pulled into a case that unravels twenty years of the town's carefully kept lies. Gideon discovers that Vane faked his death to escape blackmail by the town council, and that the sole witness to the original crime—a woman officially recorded as dead—is alive and hiding in plain sight as the archive clerk, Maren Quill. As Gideon closes in on the truth, they must choose between exposing the ledger that would destroy the town's found families or protecting the people who finally made them feel seen. In the end, Gideon finds a third path: publishing the truth with mercy, freeing Maren from her false death while letting the town reckon honestly with its past.
about_author: Emrys Underhill is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wills, deeds, and death certificates in rural New England. Their fiction is known for quiet mysteries where paperwork holds more secrets than graveyards.

chapters.title: The Weight of Absence
chapters.summary: Gideon Yarrow, POV. Called to witness the court-ordered exhumation of founder Cornelius Vane, Gideon watches the coffin open on nothing but river stones. The town's grief curdles into suspicion, and Gideon's photographic memory catches one detail no one else does: the burial permit bears a forged signature. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Rain
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Reconstructing Vane's death file from memory, Gideon finds gaps too neat to be accidental—missing coroner pages, a witness listed as deceased whose death certificate was never filed. Mayor Aldous Crane pressures them to close the case quietly. Emotional beat: the first pull between duty and curiosity.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. At the county archive, Gideon meets Maren Quill, the soft-spoken clerk whose hands shake when Vane's name surfaces. A misfiled ledger page reveals Vane withdrew his entire fortune weeks before his 'death.' Gideon realizes someone inside the archive has been editing history. Emotional beat: wary connection sparking.

chapters.title: Dead on Paper
chapters.summary: Maren Quill, POV. Revealed: Maren is Edith Vane's former housekeeper, the sole witness to the night Vane staged his death—and the council declared her dead to bury what she saw. She has lived two decades as a ghost, watching over Vane's hidden letters. Emotional beat: terror of being found warring with longing to be known.

chapters.title: What the Council Buried
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Digging into the founding families, Gideon uncovers the original crime: Vane discovered the council had burned a tenement for insurance money, killing three people. His 'death' was escape; their silence was purchased. Crane offers Gideon a promotion to forget it all. Emotional beat: loyalty to the town cracking against truth.

chapters.title: A House Full of Strangers
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The boarding-house family Maren has secretly loved for years becomes collateral—Crane suspects an informant among them and turns neighbors against neighbors. Maren must decide whether protecting them means surrendering herself. Emotional beat: found family tested by fear.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Last Page
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Following Vane's coded letters, Gideon locates the hidden ledger naming every council member who took blood money—including Crane's father. But Crane anticipates them, and Gideon is framed for evidence tampering and suspended. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: Two Ghosts at Midnight
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Maren POVs. Hunted and discredited, Gideon tracks the archive clerk through the flooded quarry tunnels where Vane once hid. They meet face to face at last—investigator and ghost—and strike a fragile pact: expose everything together, whatever it costs. Emotional beat: trust kindled in darkness.

chapters.title: Ashfall Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. At the founders' day assembly, Gideon publicly reads the ledger and Vane's confession while Maren steps forward, alive, before the whole town. Crane attempts to silence them but is undone by his own daughter, who corroborates the tenement fire. Emotional beat: catharsis—the town's lie shattering in daylight.

chapters.title: Signed in Living Ink
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Months later: the guilty are tried, Vane returns to face judgment of his own choosing, and Maren legally reclaims her name. Gideon, no longer invisible, is asked to stay as the town's records keeper beside her. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved—truth kept, family chosen, home earned.
